newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman welcomes EU farm reform outline.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman welcomes EU farm reform outline.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman welcomed the prospect Tuesday of cuts in crop support prices in the European Union.

The reductions would accompany EU expansion into eastern Europe. European Commission president Jacques Santer told the European Parliament that grain supports would be cut by 20 percent in farm reforms that are needed to add five nations to the EU.
"We respond positively to CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) reform," Glickman told reporters.

"As a general proposition, those reforms are what we have been asking them to do for a long period of time, to become more market-oriented than they have been. So, yes, we would respond positively without prejudging the specifics of it."
Santer said there would be direct compensation to grain farmers but at only half of the reduction in support rates.

EU dairy supports would be cut by 10 percent and beef supports by 30 percent. The EU anticipated five eastern European nations -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Estonia and Slovenia -- would join the union between 2001 and 2003.
